name: Xiangtan Xinchuang Government Cloud Platform / Cloud on Xiangtan
developer: Xiangtan Municipal Big Data and Industrial Innovation Development Center
notes: Municipal cloud infrastructure supporting 125 government systems; public article also identifies Hunan Big Data Industrial Park and related digital industry chain in Xiangtan. Physical datacenter capacity not disclosed.

name: Alibaba Cloud Innovation Center (Xiangtan) Big Data Industrial Base
developer: Xiangtan High-tech Zone; Alibaba Cloud; Hunan Bayun Technology
notes: Alibaba Cloud page says the Xiangtan High-tech Zone, Alibaba Cloud and Hunan Bayun jointly built the big-data industrial base, launched in July 2020; appears to be an industrial/cloud enablement base, not a large colocation datacenter.

name: Xiangxi Prefecture Big Data Center / Government Cloud Platform
developer: Xiangxi Prefecture Smart City Office / Xiangxi Prefecture Government
notes: Hunan provincial government reported about RMB 400m invested, the prefecture big-data-center computer room completed, and phase-one cloud platform infrastructure in use; later provincial statistics article confirms integration with government cloud and data-sharing platforms.

name: Furong Cloud Big Data Center
developer: Furong Cloud / China Capital Investment Management and partners
notes: Yiyang High-tech Zone facility launched operations in 2018. Planned 20,000 high-density racks, phase one 6,000 racks, T4 standard, total land about 450 mu. Yiyang 2023-2025 plan names Furong Cloud Big Data Center as the core of the city's compute support system.

name: Yiyang High-tech Zone AI Supercomputing Center Project
developer: Yiyang High-tech Zone
notes: Official investment promotion notice describes a planned AI computing center with total capacity of 20,000 high-density cabinets; exact MW not disclosed.

name: Huawei (Yongzhou) Cloud Computing Data Center
developer: Huawei Cloud; Yongzhou Economic and Technological Development Zone
notes: Introduced in April 2016, later officially online. Yongzhou government source says phase one has 13,924.92 sqm GFA, 1,000 standard server cabinets, 480,000-core cloud computing and 45P cloud storage; Hunan government says it is one of Huawei's 22 core nodes and Huawei's only node in Hunan.

name: Yueyang Cloud Data Center / China Telecom Yueyang Cloud Computing Center
developer: China Telecom Yueyang Branch
notes: Rednet reported the Yueyang big data cloud center room was completed at China Telecom Yueyang branch, marking China Telecom's cloud computing center project landing in Yueyang. Capacity not disclosed.

name: China Unicom Hunan Central-South Research Institute Yueyang Cloud Data Center (Core Office Building)
developer: China Unicom Hunan / China United Network Communications
notes: Yueyang natural resources/planning bureau published detailed-plan adjustment pre-approval for a 2024 Yueyang cloud data center/core office building project. Yueyang 2025 reply separately says the city had 7 compute centers: 5 built, 2 under construction, with over 3,200 designed racks and 9P general compute.

name: Zhangjiajie Smart City Cloud Computing Big Data Center
developer: Zhangjiajie municipal e-government / Inspur
notes: Zhangjiajie e-government construction rules require qualifying government hardware to be centrally hosted in the municipal smart-city cloud-computing big-data-center room. Inspur case material describes the center as a unified cloud resource pool for city agencies.

name: Zhangjiajie Metaverse Pilot Base Data Center / Server Room
developer: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park related project sponsors
notes: Project launched with planned investment over RMB 50m; online component includes a cultural-tourism big data center and offline component includes server integration, network integration and constant-temperature computer room. Small specialized facility; MW not disclosed.

name: China Mobile (Hunan Zhuzhou) Data Center / Big Data Center
developer: China Mobile Hunan
notes: Provincial action plan describes the facility as among South China's largest: about 300 mu site, 8 data-center rooms plus support buildings, 160,000 sqm machine-room area, planned about 30,000 racks, infrastructure investment near RMB 4bn, able to support at least 280,000 servers; phase one operational and phase two planned for completion by June 2024.

name: China Mobile (Hunan Zhuzhou) Data Center Phase II
developer: China Mobile Hunan; Hunan No.3 Engineering Co.
notes: Hunan No.3 Engineering reported municipal leaders inspected phase II civil works and reviewed phase I/II operation and construction status. Trade press says phase II started in Oct 2022, investment over RMB 1bn, two data-center buildings and support works, expected 13,000-rack capability when built.

name: Inner Mongolia Tengger Haitao Cloud Green Smart Computing Center
developer: Inner Mongolia Haitao Cloud Data Technology Co. / local Alxa partners
notes: Trade press reports the project was signed in Alxa League's Luanjingtan Ecological Migration Demonstration Zone on 2025-03-05, with RMB 4.5bn investment, a green intelligent-computing plus renewable-energy model, and planned 10,000P high-performance compute cluster. MW not disclosed.

name: Baotou Cloud Computing Center
developer: Sugon / Baotou municipal and district governments
notes: Local governments signed with Sugon in 2011-2012; report says phase one opened within half a year and became Inner Mongolia's first operating cloud-computing center project. Later China News Inner Mongolia item describes it as a commercial cloud computing center and enterprise R&D platform.

name: Baotou Rare Earth High-tech Zone Cloud Computing Big Data Center
developer: Baotou Rare Earth High-tech Zone
notes: Report sourced to Baotou Daily says the project began construction in July 2016, total investment RMB 18.995m, and phase-one acceptance covered equipment delivery, installation, debugging and infrastructure cloud deployment.

name: Baogang Industrial Internet Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Baogang / Baotou industrial internet project sponsors
notes: Reported as Baotou's first East-Data-West-Computing compute project. First batch of capacity had been operating stably for nearly one month by Oct. 2024; project includes a data center building and operations building, 10 machine-room zones, 1,358 high-density compute racks and eventual 20,000P compute scale.

name: Baotou Maifushi AI Digital Zero-Carbon Park Demonstration Base
developer: Baotou Maifushi Technology Co.
notes: Trade press citing Inner Mongolia investment project approval platform says the RMB 3bn project was filed by Baotou Rare Earth High-tech Zone Economic Development Bureau on 2026-03-04; planned March 2026-March 2029, focused on AI hardware, zero-carbon management, industrial collaboration and government intelligence.

name: JD Bayannur Cloud Computing Data Center
developer: JD.com
notes: 2012 reports say JD signed an investment framework for a RMB 2bn Bayannur cloud-computing data center, with phase one planned for 4 cloud-computing data centers, 150,000-200,000 servers, 800PB storage and 1,920THz compute. Later completion/operation could not be confirmed in this pass, so status is unknown.

name: Inner Mongolia Tianji Wulate Zhongqi Intelligent Computing Data Center
developer: Inner Mongolia Tianji Intelligent Computing Technology Co.
notes: Report says Bayannur's first intelligent-computing center project started in Wulate Zhongqi on 2026-04-11. Planned investment RMB 16bn, 200 mu site and total compute scale 50,000P; phase one RMB 430m for a 3,000P green intelligent-computing center plus energy facilities.

name: Wulate Zhongqi Zero-Carbon Port Logistics Hub 'Honggang Shujian' Intelligent Computing Project
developer: Wulate Zhongqi / project company not confirmed
notes: Trade press reports a RMB 89.9673m intelligent-computing zero-carbon port logistics hub project in Ganqimaodu, Wulate Zhongqi. Details are limited; included to mark small edge/industry compute activity in Bayannur.
